chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bakr, from Abdullah ibn Abi Sahl, from Hammad, from Abd al-Karim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three things are among the blessings: a compliant wife, righteous children, and a man who is provided with his livelihood in his own country, going to it in the morning and returning to it in the evening.'

key_terms.يَغْدُو وَيَرُوح: To go out in the morning and return in the evening (indicating local work)

ai.seo_question: What are the three sources of happiness according to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), framing domestic harmony, righteous progeny, and local sustenance as the triad of worldly felicity. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *barakah* in daily life, suggesting that economic stability within one's community reduces hardship and fosters spiritual tranquility. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Imams, linking social stability directly to individual piety and divine favor.
